question: As per the 2001 Census, what is the specific age, for a person to be called literate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3) 7 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the 2001 Census of India, a person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language is considered literate.
 
• The literacy rate is calculated by considering the population aged 7 years and above.
 
• Literacy has been a key focus area for the Indian government to improve educational outcomes.
 
• The 2001 Census marked a significant improvement in literacy rates compared to previous decades.
 
• The Census data is used to assess the impact of educational policies and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Definition:**

 
 
• Literacy is the ability to read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of educational development in a country.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Literacy is vital for social and economic development.
 
• It empowers individuals and improves quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Programs in India:**
 
 
• Numerous government initiatives aim to improve literacy rates, such as the National Literacy Mission.
 
• Programs like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan focus on universalizing elementary education.
 
 
 
• **Data Collection in Census:**
 
 
• The Census collects data on various demographic, social, and economic parameters.
 
• Literacy rate is one of the key statistics derived from Census data.
